set.cycle_notes: Annual County NOFA for housing applications (CDBG, HOME, PLHA plus 1:1 Marin Affordable Housing Fund match), run through the Neighborly portal starting with FY 2026-27. Sequence: PSC timeline meeting in December, NOFA opens mid-January, PSC and Board hearings in May and June, separate PLHA resolution once HCD confirms the calendar-year allocation. Only CDBG public services use a two-year cycle.
set.typical_award_size: 2020 five-year plan estimated $4,353,426 from HCD, each dollar matched by the County Affordable Housing Fund; Formula Round 5 award $476,762 (March 2025); 2026-27 cycle about $477,000 PLHA plus match. HCD 2024-2028 Formula Allocation NOFA estimates: CY 2024 $509,302, CY 2025 $545,537, five-year $3,183,138. Example award: $605,062 to EAH Housing in 2024 ($302,531 PLHA plus $302,531 Trust Fund). HCD now requires 40% of new PLHA for affordable owner-occupied workforce housing (up to 150% AMI in high-cost Marin), and the County noted its owner-occupied spending was trailing. FY 2026-27 round: estimated $476,762 PLHA available, $3,600,000 in PLHA requested; PSC recommended Eden Housing Oak Hill $553,524 and EAH Bayfront Terrace $400,000 (PLHA plus 1:1 match, $953,524 total), preliminary until the State confirms the 2026 allocation.
set.layering_notes: Roughly $1,000,000 a year including County match, spread across two or three projects. Marin's housing element was certified in 2025, so PLHA flows without the compliance holds seen in San Mateo. State funds trigger prevailing wage. Figures from the HCD 2024-2028 PLHA NOFA (opened), the Dec 5, 2024 PSC packet on GovDelivery (opened) and search excerpts of County pages. Audit Nov 8, 2026: June 23, 2026 Board staff report (FY 2026-27 CDBG, HOME, Housing Fund and PLHA recommendations) opened on marin.granicus.com; marincounty.gov NOFA pages return 403. The Nov 3, 2026 Housing Trust workshop report shows an $18,820,048 uncommitted Trust balance, $18,650,000 in pending requests and a Trust guidelines update planned for 2027, which may affect match availability.

set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. MHA has no project-based voucher solicitation posted on its website or procurement page, and its September 2026 Board report shows capacity committed to the Golden Gate Village and senior portfolio RAD conversions. Ask MHA directly about PBVs for specific supportive housing projects.
set.cycle_notes: No scheduled PBV cycle. MHA issues PBV solicitations only when vouchers are available (none recently); bids are posted on procurement.opengov.com/portal/marinhousing. The 2027 PHA Annual Plan comment period closed in July 2026 and the plan was due to HUD in October 2026. HAP contracts up to 20 years.
set.typical_award_size: MHA holds 496 public housing units and 2,541 Housing Choice Vouchers (3,037 combined, FY 2027 draft PHA Plan) and serves the whole county under cooperation agreements with every city. The FY 2027 plan begins converting the roughly 300-unit senior and disabled public housing portfolio (Mill Valley, San Rafael, Novato) to project-based vouchers through a RAD and Section 18 blend, and Golden Gate Village (296 units, Marin City) is converting under RAD with Burbank Housing: Phase 1 (93 units) reached a $97,600,000 financial close on Aug 19, 2026 (CMFA bonds, CDLAC allocation of $41,748,341 and about $3,985,091 in annual federal credits), RAD subsidy began Sep 1, 2026, management moved to Burbank Aug 14, 2026 and rehab runs through Feb 2028; Phase 2 (207 units) is planned as six sub-phases from 2027 to 2030; Phase 2 TEFRA for up to $160,000,000 of bonds was set for Oct 20, 2026; the full program is estimated at $266,600,000. MHA runs PBV waitlists for partner properties (Victory Village in Novato, Edgewater, Piper Court, Fireside, Toussin Senior, Vivalon Healthy Aging Campus, 1251 S. Eliseo PSH in Larkspur) but has issued no developer PBV RFP recently; 94 Emergency Housing Voucher households were told in Oct 2025 that funding ends in 2026. The County contributes $250,000 a year for MHA's resident services director and has committed more than $6,250,000 to Golden Gate Village since 2022.
set.layering_notes: MHA's capacity is going into its own RAD conversions through 2029, so new PBV awards for third-party projects are scarce; Shelter Plus Care and County-funded subsidies (Binford Road temporary rental support, $744,432 contract Dec 16, 2025) fill the gap for PSH. A HAP contract is not a prevailing wage trigger; Davis-Bacon applies to PBV construction of nine or more contract units, and RAD and public housing work carry Davis-Bacon regardless. Sources opened: MHA website pages, the FY 2027 draft PHA Plan (HUD-50075-ST), the April 14, 2026 Golden Gate Village loan staff report, Board agendas on Granicus and Patch and Local News Matters coverage of the bond approvals. Audit Nov 8, 2026: MHA website (home, procurement and 2027 Annual Plan notice pages) and the Sep 29, 2026 MHA Board agenda and Executive Director presentation on marincounty.primegov.com opened; no PBV RFP or new PBV commitments found.
